inspiration.observed_pattern: A MySQL geometry query computes pairwise Euclidean distance with squared coordinate differences, then applies SQRT, MIN, and ROUND to select the shortest distance.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Reauthored as an independently authored sensor-map proximity report. Fixed integer coordinates are paired once by point ID, POWER squares each axis difference, SQRT produces Euclidean distance, and MIN/ROUND report the nearest pair; the source table, values, aliases, and application domain are new.

fixture_notes: Sensor points 701-704 form fixed coordinate pairs; the closest pair is point 702 to 704 at distance 3; the remaining pair distances are 4, 5, 10, and sqrt(52).
determinism_notes: All point IDs, integer coordinates, pair predicate, and aggregate expression are fixed. The query has no clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent connections.
setup: CREATE TABLE sensor_points (point_id INT PRIMARY KEY, x_coord INT NOT NULL, y_coord INT NOT NULL)

steps.sql: SELECT ROUND(MIN(SQRT(POWER(left_point.x_coord - right_point.x_coord, 2) + POWER(left_point.y_coord - right_point.y_coord, 2))), 2) AS nearest_distance FROM sensor_points AS left_point JOIN sensor_points AS right_point ON left_point.point_id < right_point.point_id

checks.sql: SELECT point_id, x_coord, y_coord FROM sensor_points ORDER BY point_id
